title: [GraphKernel]Fix Kernel address Cache Table
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
> Uncomment only one ` /kind <>` line, hit enter to put that in a new line, and remove leading whitespaces from that line:

> /kind bug



**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:
This PR fixes the wrong kernel address cache table implementation.

Previously we can look up kernel address through cache table instead of searching each time. The implemention
details are in (http://gitee.com/mindspore/mindspore/blob/master/mindspore/ccsrc/runtime/device/gpu/gpu_kernel_runtime.cc).

However, the implementation of the kernel address cache table is fragile and may cause precision problem when using kernel graph optimization together. In certain models, we may get wrong kernel address with current code.

The main problem is parameter's address may change and our cache table failed to update it. Currently, the cache table build a relation map from kernel to another kernel's address, which means table's `key` is `current kernel` and `value` is `another kernel's address`. As a result, if some other developers change a kernel's address, and we don't update the address table accordingly, bugs may generate. 

This PR separates the cache table into two parts. We have a map from `current kernel` to  `another kernel` and then look up another kernel's address through its address. Because all the developers will maintain a kernel's address in its kernel info through public interface, the address in the kernel info will always be up to date. Besides, in a given graph, two nodes' relation is fixed, so we don't need to worry that a map from `current kernel` to  `another kernel` will be changed. 

This new design makes the relations more independent and avoid mixing things together. Our code will also be more robust in further development.

title: [GraphKernel]Add Address Cache Flag
body:
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:

1) If this is your first time, please read our contributor guidelines: https://gitee.com/mindspore/mindspore/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md

2) If you want to contribute your code but don't know who will review and merge, please add label `mindspore-assistant` to the pull request, we will find and do it as soon as possible.
-->

**What type of PR is this?**


kind feature


**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:
Adding a new Flag `enable_addr_cache` for graph kernel.
 
Previously we can look up kernel address through cache table instead of searching each time. The implemention 
 details are in (http://gitee.com/mindspore/mindspore/blob/master/mindspore/ccsrc/runtime/device/gpu/gpu_kernel_runtime.cc).

However, the implementation of the kernel address cache table is fragile and may cause precision problem when using kernel graph optimization together. In certain models, we may get wrong kernel address with current code.

This PR adds a control flag for the kernel address cache function. People can choose to use it or not through the flag.

The default value for  `enable_addr_cache` is `false` ,which means we close this function by default and people can open it by set 
`context.set_context(graph_kernel_flags="--opt_level=1 --enable_addr_cache")`.

body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind feature
Support runtime Export of Models in quantization type other than the default

**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:
To allow the user to save a model in quantization type he chooses regradless of the quantization in the convert.
This feature may be relevant especially in the future, where users can create models on device and then export them as quantized models

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
<!-- 
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
-->
Fixes #

**Special notes for your reviewers**:
We want to keep the Export process under CI, both export, as well as loading and running of quantized models. However, the accuracy of quantized models lowers. 
We added a flag to MarkAccuracy method to keep track of accuracy but not fail the test in case accuracy is too big. This flag is turned on for on-device quantized models
The accuracy error itself following quantization is not too big (~6-10%) -- but we want to keep the original threshold ~0.5 for unquantized models as low as possible to keep bit-exactness with MS cloud

**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:
check the Optimizer parameters be a list

At present, the parameters are not strictly required to be iteration, so the error message is not clear and
changed when operate on parameters.

For example:
If parameters is a Tensor, the expected error is a type error. But list(Tensor) and list(Parameter) + Tensor will run the Tensor operation, the error message is all about the Tensor operation and will changed if Tensor's operation changed.

So we check parameters should be Iteration and convert the parameters to a list before operating on it.

**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:

1. Change the permission of cache-created shared memory from `666` to `600`, per the request of a HQ security team. This will disable multiple users from sharing the same cache server.

title: MD Profiling Summary Support with Bottleneck Op
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind task


**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:

Need to fulfill the requirement to provide MindData profiling summary information based on the existing input files.

The existing 3 input MindData profiling files are: (for example device_id=0)
- device_queue_profiling_0.txt  or dataset_iterator_profiling_0.txt (depending on environment)
- minddata_cpu_utilization_0.json
- pipeline_profiling_0.json

The output needs to include summary pipeline information, including possible bottleneck op in the pipeline, plus suggestion to resolve this possible bottleneck.
The output should also include analyzed pipeline information which are used to determine a potential bottleneck op in a MindData pipeline.

For flexibility, the MindData analyzed summary output is provided in the following formats:
- returned as dictionary
- JSON output file created with filename minddata_pipeline_summary_0.json
- CSV output file created with filename minddata_pipeline_summary_0.csv

**EXAMPLE OUTPUT:** 
Example minddata_pipeline_summary_0.json output:
```
{"pipeline_ops": ["DeviceQueue(id=0)", "Batch(id=1)", "Shuffle(id=2)", "Map(id=3)", "Map(id=4)", "Map(id=5)", "Map(id=6)", "Map(id=7)", "Mnist(id=8)"], 
"op_names": ["DeviceQueue", "Batch", "Shuffle", "Map", "Map", "Map", "Map", "Map", "Mnist"], 
"op_ids": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8], 
"num_workers": [1, 8, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 8], 
"queue_average_size": [-1, 44.6, 10.5, 0.67, 0.12, 0.14, 0.25, 2.68, 11.55], 
"queue_utilization_pct": [-1, 69.69, 65.62, 4.19, 0.75, 0.88, 1.56, 16.75, 18.05], 
"queue_empty_freq_pct": [-1, 24.68, 20.13, 33.12, 97.4, 96.1, 94.16, 83.12, 81.82], 
"children_ids": [[1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [6], [7], [8], []], 
"parent_id": [-1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7], 
"avg_cpu_pct": [37.8, 5.91, 5.3, 20.65, 16.56, 16.71, 22.97, 13.93, 13.18], 
"per_batch_time": [2.736], 
"avg_cpu_pct_per_worker": [37.8, 0.74, 5.3, 20.65, 16.56, 16.71, 22.97, 13.93, 1.65], 
"bottleneck_warning": ["Mnist(id=8) has output queue that is empty 81.82% of the time. This is more than the threshold of 70.0%. Operators with frequent empty output queues can cause the next operator to be waiting on it most of the time."], 
"bottleneck_suggestion": ["Increase prefetch_size for Mnist(id=8)."]}
```

**DESIGN NOTES:** 

The class  MinddataProfilingAnalyzer has been provided in a new file  **minddata_analyzer.py**  within mindspore/profiler/parser to be invoked by the Profiler class (independent of what is done in MinddataPipelineParser).  
The current implementation is solely in Python (but the processing to process the MindData information can be in C++ in the future, as per long term direction).

_Bottleneck algorithm:_ 
The initial bottleneck algorithm is the following:
- The algorithm below is triggered only if MD is slower than ME. That happens if DeviceQueue’s input queue is Z% empty.
- Leaf: Leaf is bottleneck if its output queue is only X% full.  If its CPU/num_workers is above Y%, suggest user to increase num_workers. Otherwise, suggest user to increase prefetch_size.
- Map: Map is bottleneck if its CPU/num_workers is above Y%, suggest user to increase num_workers
- Batch: : Batch is bottleneck if its CPU/num_workers is above Y%, suggest user to increase num_workers. Batch is also bottleneck if CPU/num_workers is low and its input queue is empty. Suggest user to increase prefetch_size.


**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #  https://gitee.com/mindspore/mindspore/issues/I3R8D1


**Special notes for your reviewers**:

Items to be done in subsequent PRs:

- Augment and improve this initial bottleneck algorithm, including the bottleneck threshold constants, and include input from more workloads.

- Reduce output formats (dictionary, JSON and CSV) to just one of these, depending on user feedback.

- Reduce the sampling range from the metrics output queue pipeline data (e.g. take the middle 50% to 80%).

- Correct the conditions when the device trace file is found.  Current code expects:
  - On CPU, the filename is 'dataset_iterator_profiling_<device_id>.txt'.
  - On GPU and Ascend, the filename is 'device_trace_profiling_<device_id>.txt'.
  If the device trace file is not found, then an error is NOT raised, but MD analyze processing continues (but this means that per_batch_time is not computed).

- Create Python Unit Test to verify the output - namely files are returned and sanity check for some/all of the keys returned

>
> /kind bug
> /kind task
/kind feature


**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:
To save the memory used for 13B PanGu-Alpha, the parameters are initialized with float16 so that the model can run predicition in One Ascend Card. Also, for training the model can use float16 parameters and use float32 as optimizer's dtype.

The main changes are as follows:

1. Initilize the net with FP16 (except for layer norm and embeddings)
2. Initlize the optimizer's state as fp32, as fp16 maybe easily overflow.(Only support Adam Optimizer)
3. Add args to control whether init model with FP16 or Fp32.
4. Set full batch to be False, as the dataset is data parallel.
5. Add cast op for adam optimizer, if the param does not need to update itself( gradient is fp32, so a cast is neeeded).

title: [GraphKernel]Fix circle bugs
body:
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:

1) If this is your first time, please read our contributor guidelines: https://gitee.com/mindspore/mindspore/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md

2) If you want to contribute your code but don't know who will review and merge, please add label `mindspore-assistant` to the pull request, we will find and do it as soon as possible.
-->

**What type of PR is this?**

> /kind bug



**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:

There were some DFS termination conditions during circle check when we cluster nodes (http://gitee.com/mindspore/mindspore/blob/master/mindspore/ccsrc/backend/optimizer/graph_kernel/graph_kernel_cluster.cc). These conditions can make our algorithm efficient, however, we found two of them not robust enough. They cause compile failure when we try more models. The circle problem in tinyBert(#I3R2GN)  is an example.

This PR makes two changes to make it safer and guarantee no circle exists.



 

### Problem #1

During circle check, this line adds a DFS termination condition when   **other cluster's id < current cluster's first Node's id** 

```
// so if the node_id is less than the minimal candidate, a cycle cannot be formed from this node.
if (candidates_->empty() || node_id < *candidates_->begin()) {
          return EXCLUDE;
 }
```

Link: (http://gitee.com/mindspore/mindspore/blob/master/mindspore/ccsrc/backend/optimizer/graph_kernel/graph_kernel_cluster.cc#L294)

However, this condition is not sufficient.  Let's see an example:
Originally we define Cluster id as the smallest Node id in it. Suppose we have these relations:        

  Node id1-->Node id2(not clusterable)  -->       Node id3 -->  Node id8
         \  \-->Node id7 <-- Node id4(not clusterable)<--/   
![enter image description here](https://images.gitee.com/uploads/images/2021/0513/145818_e41fdfa2_8990305.jpeg "{D566D908-E961-45E1-8D55-867F43D6778C}.png.jpg")
                     
And we may cluster them as:
 **Cluster id1 : {Node id1,  Node id7}
Cluster id2 : {Node id2}
Cluster id3 : {Node id3, Node id8}
Cluster id4  :{Node id4}** 

So here circle exists:

 **Cluster id1--> Cluster id2 --> Cluster id3--> Custer id4 --> Cluster id1** 


The original condition failed to find the circle because we terminate the circle check when   **other cluster's id < current cluster's first Node's id**   .  If current cluster is Cluster  **id4**  and, when we check Cluster  **id3** ,  **id3**  is smaller than the first node's id ( **id4** ) of Cluster  **id4**   and we just stop the check and suppose there is no circle.

This kind of check is unsafe and we change the condition as:


```
// so if the other node's cluster's max node id is less than the minimal candidate, a circle cannot be formed from this node.
 if (candidates_.empty() || graph_->GetClusterMaxNodeId(node_id) < *candidates_.begin()) {
          return EXCLUDE;
        }
```
Now we only terminate circle check when **other node's cluster's max node id <current cluster's first Node's id** 

If current cluster is Cluster  **Id4**  and, when we check Cluster  **id3** , Cluster  **Id3**'s largest node is **id8** ,**id8**  is not smaller than the first node's id ( **id4** ) of Cluster  **id4**  and we go deep and continue to check the circle, eventually finding the circle.


### Problem #2
The logic to find clusters is to find potential candidates first and exclude some members in the candidates which may cause circles.

Originally,  **set**  is used to store all the candidates.

```
std::set<size_t> GraphKernelCluster::FindCandidates(size_t basenode_id) {

```
(http://gitee.com/mindspore/mindspore/blob/master/mindspore/ccsrc/backend/optimizer/graph_kernel/graph_kernel_cluster.cc#L330)

When we iterated candidates one by one, we followed ascending order rather than DFS order.  Following ascending order may fail to exclude some members which should be excluded. So this PR chooses **vector** to store all the candidates in DFS order.

Here are the new codes:
```
std::vector<size_t> GraphKernelCluster::FindCandidates(size_t basenode_id) {

```

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
<!-- 
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
-->
Fixes #I3R2GN

title: Evaluate the func graph in simulative stack, not to call recursively.
body:
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:

1) If this is your first time, please read our contributor guidelines: https://gitee.com/mindspore/mindspore/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md

2) If you want to contribute your code but don't know who will review and merge, please add label `mindspore-assistant` to the pull request, we will find and do it as soon as possible.
-->

**What type of PR is this?**
> Uncomment only one ` /kind <>` line, hit enter to put that in a new line, and remove leading whitespaces from that line:
>
> /kind bug
> /kind task
> /kind feature

/kind feature

**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:
We use Evaluator to infer the func graph and other fundamental operations.
When we evaluate the func graph, including FuncGraph and MetaFuncGraph,
we evaluate each nodes in the graph one by one.
If the node is a func graph call, it will bind a new Evaluator and triger its running.
So, we may see Evaluator.Run() is called recursively in a long long call stack.
If the stack size exceeds the limit of Linux&Windows system, core dump would just happen.

---
After this PR, we'll evaluate the func graph in simulative stack, not to call recursively.
- Handle FuncGraphAbstractClosure with stack frame, not Evaluator call.
- Not handle MetaFuncGraphAbstractClosure by now.

If it's FuncGraphAbstractClosure, we'll launch a stack frame routine in its Evaluator.Run().

---
The result is:
- Resnet:
  27 -> 5
  ( function call max depth: 27, simulate call max depth: 22)
- Bert:
  121 -> 6
  (function call max depth: 121, simulate call max depth: 115)


**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.

This PR is to add a new function to Auto-parallel, namely sharding propagation, which propagates from configured-ops to non-configured-ops with the goal of zero redistribution communication cost:
1) users configure sharding strategies for operators;
2) framework will propagate the strategies from configured-ops to non-configured-ops using BFS;

title: Demo of using cache to improve perf for dataset-on-nfs scenarios
body:
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:

1) If this is your first time, please read our contributor guidelines: https://gitee.com/mindspore/mindspore/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md

2) If you want to contribute your code but don't know who will review and merge, please add label `mindspore-assistant` to the pull request, we will find and do it as soon as possible.
-->

**What type of PR is this?**
> Uncomment only one ` /kind <>` line, hit enter to put that in a new line, and remove leading whitespaces from that line:
>
> /kind bug
> /kind task
> /kind feature


**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:

This PR provides another cache usage demo in model_zoo. We found that if the dataset is located on remote network storages such as NFS, caching the dataset might help to improve the training performance. Therefore, this PR provides a separate script `run_train_nfs_cache.sh` for running training with a dataset located on NFS, which by default enables caching for better performance.

Some perf data collected with mobilenetv2 4p training on GPU, Imagenet dataset on NFS:

|                                     |cache:True     |cache:False    |
|-------------------------------------|---------------|---------------|
|Memory usage of cache server         |137.612GB      |               |
|First epoch time                     |3384.51s       |1649.18s       |
|Mean epoch time EXCLUDING first epoch|421.90s        |708.58s        |
|Per step time EXCLUDING first epoch  |197.612ms      |331.885ms      |

With cache, the first epoch time increases significantly due to cache writing overhead, but all later epochs can benefit from caching the dataset in memory. Therefore, the more epochs, the more cache case shows benefits due to per-step-time savings.

主要是用于在r1.2分支上添加Faster_RCNN网络（以Resnet50,101,152作为backbone），Faster_RCNN网络复现之后在mindspore r1.2版本进行训练以及测试。Faster_RCNN网络实现了一个two-stage结构的目标检测网络框架，其中主体结构包含4个部分，包括由Resnet构成的网络主干，由FPN（Feature Paramid Network）构成的高分辨率特征融合模块，由RPN（Region Proposal Network）构成的兴趣区域（ROI）检测模块，以及由卷积和全连接层构成的分类和位置调整模块（RCNN）。实验结果表明在COCO数据集目标检测任务取得较好性能与较高精度。

body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug

**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:
When creating the new GKDropout, the original process used the Dropout's input's kernel_info to infer the kernel_info of new node. But if the input is a Tensor, then it hasn't kernel_info, which causes the GKDropout's input_kernel_info to be invalid.
In this submit, I manually set the kernel_infos to ensure they are always valid.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #I3OW0G

title: Evaluate the func graph in simulative stack, not to call recursively.
body:
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:

1) If this is your first time, please read our contributor guidelines: https://gitee.com/mindspore/mindspore/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md

2) If you want to contribute your code but don't know who will review and merge, please add label `mindspore-assistant` to the pull request, we will find and do it as soon as possible.
-->

**What type of PR is this?**
> Uncomment only one ` /kind <>` line, hit enter to put that in a new line, and remove leading whitespaces from that line:
>
> /kind bug
> /kind task
> /kind feature

/kind feature

**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:
We use Evaluator to infer the func graph and other fundamental operations.
When we evaluate the func graph, including FuncGraph and MetaFuncGraph,
we evaluate each nodes in the graph one by one.
If the node is a func graph call, it will bind a new Evaluator and triger its running.
So, we may see Evaluator.Run() is called recursively in a long long call stack.
If the stack size exceeds the limit of Linux&Windows system, core dump would just happen.

---
After this PR, we'll evaluate the func graph in simulative stack, not to call recursively.
- Handle FuncGraphAbstractClosure with stack frame, not Evaluator call.
- Not handle MetaFuncGraphAbstractClosure by now.

If it's FuncGraphAbstractClosure, we'll launch a stack frame routine in its Evaluator.Run().

---
The result is:
- Resnet:
  27 -> 5
  ( function call max depth: 27, simulate call max depth: 22)
- Bert:
  121 -> 6
  (function call max depth: 121, simulate call max depth: 115)

title: Fix segment input/output caculation
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug


**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:
After this PR: https://e.gitee.com/mind_spore/repos/mindspore/mindspore/pulls/14580
When graph is partitioned, we may got wrong inputs/outputs for a segment. for example:

```
segment1:
  ...
  x = MatMul(a, b)
  ..
```

```
segment2:
  ...
  UpdateState(u, c, x)
  ...
```

Because MatMul in segment1 is used by segment2, we will incorrectly include `x` in the outputs of segment1,
and include `x` in the the inputs of segment2;
To fix this, we exclude `x` from the outputs of segment if it only used as an additional input of a UpdateState.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #I3ONA3

title: Officially support caching over MindRecord dataset
body:
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:

1) If this is your first time, please read our contributor guidelines: https://gitee.com/mindspore/mindspore/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md

2) If you want to contribute your code but don't know who will review and merge, please add label `mindspore-assistant` to the pull request, we will find and do it as soon as possible.
-->

**What type of PR is this?**
> Uncomment only one ` /kind <>` line, hit enter to put that in a new line, and remove leading whitespaces from that line:
>
> /kind bug

/kind task
> /kind feature


**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:

With PR [#15125](https://gitee.com/mindspore/mindspore/pulls/15125), `MindRecordOp` functions in a similar way as other mappable leaf ops, it creates a `MindRecordSamplerRT` in its constructor and uses this sampler for sampling.

To make `MindRecordOp` work with cache, this sampler has to be taken from `MindRecordOp` and to be given to `CacheLookupOp`, so the final execution tree should look like this:
```
MindRecordSamplerRT --> CacheLookupOp ------------
				|                |
				|             CacheMergeOp  -->
				|                |
                        MindRecordOp  ------------
```
The procedure of injecting cache-related ops and adjusting samplers is implemented in `CacheTransformPass`. But the optimization pass works on IR tree instead of the execution tree, it works like this:
```
Sampler IR
  |
Mappable Leaf IR (cache = some_cache) 

After cache transform pass:

Sampler IR --> CacheLookup IR -----------
                    |                   |
                    |                 CacheMerge IR -->
                    |                   |
             Mappable Leaf IR -----------
```

So to let `CacheTransformPass` work with `MindRecord` IR, we have to create the corresponding IR class for `MindRecordSamplerRT`, namely `MindRecordSamplerObj`. During `CacheTransformPass`, this sampler IR will be taken from `MindRecordNode` and be plugged into `CacheLookupNode`. Finally, when building, this IR object will be used to create a runtime `MindRecordSamplerRT` object.


Summary of changes in this PR:
1. Added cache argument for `MindRecord` dataset, in both python and c++ API.
2. Created the corresponding IR class for `MindRecordSamplerRT`, namely `MindRecordSamplerObj`.
3. Removed the blocking code from `CacheTransformPass`, and allow `CacheTransformPass` to also work with MindRecord
4. When building, `MindRecordSamplerObj::SamplerBuild()` not only creates a runtime `MindRecordSamplerRT` sampler object, but also creates a `ShardReader`, which is also needed to construct `MindRecordOp`. Therefore, A method（`GetShardReader()`）is provided to let the caller acquire the unique pointer of the newly created `ShardReader` object.
5. Added c++ and python unit test cases
6. Fix an issue in `ShardTaskList::TaskListSwap()` which can cause test case failure
7. Some code cleanup

-->

/kind task
> /kind feature


**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:
Adds MD Cropper: end goal is to allow customers ship their code base with a smaller MD Lite library. The library in this case will only contain the required code, and extra ops (which are not used in their code base) are removed.

It contains 2 major parts:
1.  **cropper_configure.py** : this code should be run only once. It would write to disk the dependencies of each file in MD (dependencies.txt). It also maintains the entry point for each op in associations.txt.
2.  **crop.sh** : where given the user code file(s) as argument(s), the script (along with  **parser.py** ,  **build_lib.py**  and  **CMakeLists.txt** ) will create the new cropped MD Lite library specific to the user code provided. This code needs to be run every time the user changes their code so as proper ops/functionalities of MD will be kept in the cropped MD Library.

<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:

1) If this is your first time, please read our contributor guidelines: https://gitee.com/mindspore/mindspore/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md

2) If you want to contribute your code but don't know who will review and merge, please add label `mindspore-assistant` to the pull request, we will find and do it as soon as possible.
-->

**What type of PR is this?**
> Uncomment only one ` /kind <>` line, hit enter to put that in a new line, and remove leading whitespaces from that line:
>
/kind bug


**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:
User defined TrainStepWrap many contains more than one grad-net, such as `wide&deep net`:
```python
def construct(self, batch_ids, batch_wts, label):
        '''
        Construct wide and deep model
        '''
        weights_w = self.weights_w
        weights_d = self.weights_d
        loss_w, loss_d = self.network(batch_ids, batch_wts, label)
        sens_w = P.Fill()(P.DType()(loss_w), P.Shape()(loss_w), self.sens)
        sens_d = P.Fill()(P.DType()(loss_d), P.Shape()(loss_d), self.sens)
        grads_w = self.grad_w(self.loss_net_w, weights_w)(batch_ids, batch_wts,
                                                          label, sens_w)
        grads_d = self.grad_d(self.loss_net_d, weights_d)(batch_ids, batch_wts,
                                                          label, sens_d)
        if self.reducer_flag:
            grads_w = self.grad_reducer_w(grads_w)
            grads_d = self.grad_reducer_d(grads_d)
        return F.depend(loss_w, self.optimizer_w(grads_w)), F.depend(loss_d,
                                                                     self.optimizer_d(grads_d))
```

In Graph mode, grad_w and grad_d will be combined into one graph. But in PyNative mode, there will be two graphs. So the index in `all_reduce_fusion_config` many be greater than grad count in the grad-net graph.

/kind bug
> /kind task
> /kind feature


**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:
Fixes the issue in GPU when the debugger at each iteration suspends each graph instead of doing the suspension once per each iteration. Without this PR in a multi graph model, the user has to click multiple times to go to the next step (once per graph in the run graph list). body:
**What type of PR is this?**
> /kind task


**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:
`BatchNorm` operator has five inputs and in yolov3 network, the first input may be `float16` and the rest four inputs be `float32`. In this case, `BatchNorm` will not be expanded because an exception will be raised due to the type inconsistency.
This pr adds type cast in batchnorm expander to support the above case.


**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

title: [GraphKernel] fix bug of invalid data type or format when set node info
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
> /kind bug


**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:
在构造新节点的时候，需要设置节点的node info（主要是输入输出tye、format），原先是通过调用`AnfAlgo::GetOutputDeviceDataType`函数获取节点的输入node info，当节点的输入是Tensor类型时，比如：
```
%2([CNode]40686) = Cast(Tensor(shape=[], dtype=Float32, value= 65504)) primitive_attrs: {...}
      : (<Tensor[Float32]x[const vector][]>) -> (<Tensor[Float16]x[const vector][]>)
      : (<Float32xDefaultFormat[const vector][]>) -> (<Float16xDefaultFormat[const vector][]>)
```
`Cast`的输入是Tensor类型，通过`AnfAlgo::GetOutputDeviceDataType`函数获取的是`kTypeUnknown`无效类型。实际上，新节点的输入node info可以从原先的节点中获取到。
该pr修改node info获取方式，从原先节点中获取必要的node info，并一次性传给`SetNodeInfo`函数，用于设置新生成节点的node info。


**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #https://gitee.com/mindspore/mindspore/issues/I3O67V?from=project-issue

title: gpu inference syupport multi-outputs
body:
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:

1) If this is your first time, please read our contributor guidelines: https://gitee.com/mindspore/mindspore/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md

2) If you want to contribute your code but don't know who will review and merge, please add label `mindspore-assistant` to the pull request, we will find and do it as soon as possible.
-->

**What type of PR is this?**
> /kind bug


**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:
Gpu inference will failed when graph output num > 1.

- The frontend IR as follows:
    ```
    %0 = SquareSumAll(x1, x2)
    return(%0)
    ```
    It return only 1 output, while Serving expect 2. 

- Solutuon:
    - Insert `MakeTuple` before return node. 
    ```
    %0 = SquareSumAll(x1, x2)
    %1 = MakeTuple(%0)
    return(%1)
    ```

    - It will insert `TupleGetItem` in backend common pass. It will flatten to 2 output and are consistent with Serving expection.
    ```
    %0 = SquareSumAll(x1, x2)
    %1 = TupleGetItem(%0, 0)
    %2 = TupleGetItem(%0, 1)
    %3 = MakeTuple(%1, %2)
    return(%3)
    ```
